name: top
description: An interactive, continuously updating view of processes and system resource usage, built into every distribution.

flags.description: h help, k kill, r renice, 1 per-core CPUs, M sort by memory, P sort by CPU, q quit.
Batch mode for logging to a file.

examples.output:

Tasks: 231 total,   1 running, 230 sleeping
%Cpu(s):  4.2 us,  1.1 sy, 94.7 id
MiB Mem :  15932 total,   8420 free,   3102 used
  PID USER   %CPU %MEM  COMMAND
 1187 mysql  45.0 18.3  mysqld
examples.explanation: Header shows uptime, load averages (1/5/15 min), CPU breakdown (us=user, sy=system, id=idle, wa=waiting on I/O), and memory. The process list is sorted by CPU by default.
Monitors only the web server user's processes.
Inside top: sorts by memory usage. P sorts by CPU. Press 1 to expand each CPU core.

about: Load average deserves attention: values near or above your CPU core count indicate saturation. In the memory line, "available" (not "free") is the realistic figure — Linux uses spare RAM for caches and releases it on demand. Press h inside top for the full key list.
useCases: Kill or renice processes without leaving the monitor.
Watch system health during load tests.
mistakes: Worrying about low "free" memory — cached memory is available on demand; look at "available".
